key_insight: A single compressibility number Π organizes steady gas compression across three inlet controls, while pressure curvature reveals migrating compression pulses during relaxation.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps interpret pressure, volumetric-flux, and mass-flux control in gas chromatography and underground hydrogen storage.
method: Nondimensionalize the isothermal porous medium equation using Π.
Derive a convergent perturbation series in β = 2Π/(1 + 2Π) for all three inlet controls.
Analyze relaxation eigenmodes and pressure curvature to resolve transient compression.
evidence_signal: Numerical solutions over 10⁻² ≤ Π ≤ 10³ show boundary-condition-dependent low-Π diffusivity plateaus and effective pressure-squared diffusivity scaling as Π¹ᐟ² at high Π.
watch_item: The results assume isothermal flow, and the outlet boundary layer narrows as Π⁻¹, demanding finer numerical resolution at high compressibility.
paper_title: Compressible gas flow through porous media under forced pressure and fluxes: compressibility number and pressure curvature
